description: Mint a short-lived, repository-scoped HTTPS clone credential (a deploy token) for a sandbox or CI box that has no PAT. By default it returns NO token: {id, exchangeUrl, exchangeExpiresAt, gitConfig, url}. Run the gitConfig lines right before the first clone/fetch (the URL is single-use and dies in 60 s) and git fetches the token itself, so it never enters your transcript. Read-only by default; `read_only: false` asks for push access and is granted only if you have write access. Expires in 2 h by default (`expires_in_hours`, max 24). Needs owner / collaborator / team / org access to the repo (public read is not enough) and 'repo' scope. Audit-logged. Pass `token_id` (an id this tool returned) for a fresh exchange URL for the same grant; each exchange rotates the secret. `deliver: "token"` returns a read-only secret in the result instead (refused for push access: a push-capable secret in an agent's transcript outlives the run). Revoke the grant with merjax_revoke_token {type: "deploy", id}.

deliver.description: "exchange" (default): a single-use 60 s URL git's credential helper spends — the secret never appears here. "token": a read-only secret in this result (refused with read_only: false).

expires_in_hours.description: Lifetime in hours (default 2, max 24, min 5 minutes)

owner.description: Repo owner — username or organisation slug

read_only.description: Default true. false = clone AND push (requires write access).

title.description: Where the token will be used (default 'agent clone (MCP)')

token_id.description: A fresh exchange URL for this existing grant (one you created) instead of a new grant.

name: merjax_create_deploy_token
